market_context.summary: One supply shock is driving four markets. Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities forced a temporary suspension of some operations and WTI closed 97.19 on 2026-09-09, +4.47% and its highest since May. That fed straight into rates: the 10-year traded ~4.85%, its highest since October/November 2023 (FRED's last official print 4.80% on 2026-09-08), against 3.63% effective fed funds, and market-implied odds of a HIKE at the 2026-09-16 FOMC jumped to roughly 68% from about 40% a week earlier. The curve at 10y-2y +0.40 with the front end unmoved says the repricing is term premium and inflation, not growth. Regime is mixed rather than risk-off because the repricing has not yet reached the equity index: SPY 762.40 is only 2.2% off its high and rolling over rather than breaking, energy is the one sector at its highs (XLE 65.31, 0.9% off), gold is firm above its SMA50 while nominal yields make multi-year highs — the fiscal/debasement tell — and bitcoin is in an uptrend, not weak (IBIT above both averages, 4.9% off its high). The practical consequence for today is the correlation cap: most of what looks like several energy and rates ideas is one bet on the oil price, and almost every sector is pinned at an extreme where reward-to-risk dies.

watchlist.note: CUT BY THE RED TEAM from rank 1 / conviction 5, and it is the best-researched idea in the report — the 8-K was independently re-fetched and every term the page claims is exactly right: warrant for up to 25,000,000 shares at $161.26, vesting on execution of commercial arrangements, binding purchase orders and actual purchases of QTI server chip products up to a maximum of $60 billion in payments, 3,750,000 shares vested on issuance. The thesis is falsifiable, the invalidation is stated in non-price terms, and at 15.5x trailing with 26 of 49 analysts still at hold the edge is demonstrably NOT priced. It is demoted on its levels, both of which lean the same way. (1) The bear case of $130 sits ABOVE the 121.99 the stock actually traded within the last 120 days — and that print was made BEFORE this agreement existed, so in the very scenario the bear case describes (the ramp never converts) the deal's option value is zero and the handset base is additionally impaired: the honest bear is at or below 121.99, not above it. At a 122 bear the ratio is (300-174)/(174-122) = 2.42, under the 2.5 long_term floor. A bear case lifted to flatter a ratio is the same free manoeuvre as a stop walked in, and nothing mechanical checks it. (2) The same 8-K discloses that the warrant EXPIRES 2036-09-03 — a ten-year vesting window the page omitted while key_risk affirmatively stated 'the timeline is undisclosed'. Ten years to place $60B is ~$6B/yr against ~$40B of revenue: real, but it makes the $300 target's implied FY29 re-rate to 19x an uncited ~$16 EPS considerably more of a stretch than the page allowed. Soft target and soft bear on the same idea is why this is demoted rather than downgraded.
watchlist.trigger: The idea's own second tranche: 161.26 or below, the warrant strike, where a $300 target against a 122 bear is 3.53:1 and clears the long_term floor with room. Or a cited FY28-29 EPS estimate that anchors the $300 rather than assuming it. Do not buy the first tranche at 174.
watchlist.demotion_reason: bear case set above the last pre-deal traded price; at an honest 122 bear the ratio is 2.42 against a 2.5 long_term floor, and the 8-K's undisclosed-to-the-page 2036 warrant expiry makes the target's implied ramp aggressive too

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:27 ET, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed. Seven candidate lines resolve to seven distinct symbols; BCC was captured twice and the later line wins, which raises its conviction from 3 to 4 to match its three evidence kinds.

WHY FOUR OF SEVEN IDEAS ARE EXITS. This is the shape of today's tape, not thin research. The open book was carrying four broken theses — TLT on a duration rally, BCC on a housing recovery, LULU and NKE on consumer turnarounds — and closing them is the highest-value work available. TLT is the urgent one and its rank understates that: the position is a duration long into an 08:30 CPI print tomorrow with hike odds at 68%, and the exit should be at the open regardless of where it sits on this list. LULU is settled by the company's own numbers (a third FY26 guidance cut on 2026-09-03, Q3 revenue guided -10% to -11% y/y). NKE is the weakest of the four and says so on its own page: no new NIKE-specific information, only price, and its late-September fiscal Q1 date is NOT on the fetched calendar and is not treated as dated. Position updates are not new risk and do not count against the idea count.

WHY ONLY THREE NEW POSITIONS. One shock drives four markets — Middle East supply loss to WTI $97 to inflation to 68% hike odds to a 4.85% 10-year — so the correlation cap bit hard, and almost every sector is pinned at an extreme where reward-to-risk dies. Six ideas were rejected on arithmetic alone (XLE, XOM, LMT, LEU, GDX, BTC) and the failure was identical each time: no defensible target between the price and the nearest real level. The three that cleared are diversified by driver — QCOM on AI datacenter silicon, HAL on oil services, URA on uranium — and URA's overlap with the open CCJ long is flagged on the idea itself, to be sized as one position rather than two.

RATIOS AND STOPS, RECOMPUTED FROM THE FINAL LEVELS RATHER THAN CARRIED OVER. QCOM 2.86 ((300-174)/(174-130)) against the 2.5 long-term floor; URA 2.98 with a 2.35 ATR stop against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor; HAL 2.06 with a 2.83 ATR stop against the 2.0 ATR stock floor. HAL is the one ratio close to its floor, 3% above it, so it deserves the suspicion this report applies to clustered ratios: what argues it is not fitted is the order of work recorded in the notes — the 34.00 stop was set from the SMA50 at 34.20 first and the target checked afterwards, and the 43.59 target IS the 120-day high rather than an extension beyond it. Both new swing stops clear their floors with room and neither was tightened to lift a ratio. ATR14 was re-pulled at synthesis to confirm: HAL 1.11, URA 1.73.

PRICES. Every figure is the 2026-09-09 16:00 ET close, re-quoted at synthesis and unchanged. The market was pre-open throughout both phases, so a prior close is the freshest honest equity price here, not stale data. Nothing was estimated.

WHAT COULD NOT BE REACHED. No event-contract idea was possible: Kalshi returned count:0 for both "Fed" and "CPI", and with hike odds at 68% into tomorrow's print that was the single cleanest expression available today — it could not be priced without inventing a number. No index or futures quotes worked all run (spx, ndx, dow, rut, VIX, es, nq, DXY, gold, wti all failed), so no volatility or dollar reading informed any idea and ETF proxies were substituted for the regime read. No options-implied move for any finalist (yahoo-options returned HTTP 401 on HAL). NUVL has a real 2026-09-18 PDUFA and no obtainable price from any source, so it was rejected on the never-fabricate-a-number rule rather than on its thesis. No intraday idea, deliberately: today's only dated catalyst is tomorrow's 08:30 CPI, ORCL and ADBE report after tonight's close, and there is no gap to fade — an intraday idea today would be a general lean dressed as a setup. No small-cap idea; that lane was hunted and empty.

SOURCES THAT FAILED: yahoo (429 rate-limited throughout, 401 on the options endpoint), finnhub indices (CFD subscription required), stooq (404 on all index symbols), alphavantage (no API key), Kalshi (empty result set), nasdaq short-interest (read timeout on ORCL), cnbc.com (403 to direct fetch — search snippets were used and are cited as such on the TLT and BCC ideas).

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS FROM RESEARCH STAND. Gold is NOT at new highs: GLD 403.35 is 10.1% off its 120-day high of 448.70 and below its SMA20, though still above its SMA50, so the debasement read holds directionally only. And crypto is NOT weak: that was written off a single -1.3% day, while IBIT sits above both averages 4.9% off its high.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut 2 of 7, downgraded 1, fixed levels and citations on the survivor. Five recommendations remain: one new position and four exits.

CUT QCOM (was rank 1, conviction 5). The research is the best in this report and I re-fetched the 8-K to check it: every term on the page is exactly right, and the edge is genuinely not priced (15.5x trailing, 26 of 49 analysts still at hold). It is demoted on its levels, both of which lean the same way. The $130 bear case sits ABOVE the 121.99 the stock traded within the last 120 days, and that print pre-dates the agreement — so in the very scenario the bear describes, the deal's option value is zero and the handset base is additionally impaired. On an honest 122 bear the ratio is 2.42 against the 2.5 long_term floor. A bear case lifted to clear a floor is the same free manoeuvre as a stop walked in, and unlike a stop nothing mechanical checks it. Separately, the same 8-K discloses the warrant expires 2036-09-03 — a ten-year window the page omitted while key_risk stated 'the timeline is undisclosed'. Ten years to place $60B is ~$6B/yr on ~$40B of revenue, which makes the $300 target's implied FY29 re-rate to 19x an uncited ~$16 EPS a bigger stretch than the page allowed. Soft target and soft bear on one idea is a demotion, not a downgrade. Its own accumulation plan gives the trigger: 161.26, the warrant strike, where the ratio is 3.53:1.

CUT URA (was rank 6, conviction 3). Its counter_argument concedes the strongest bear case — that the 20-31% de-rating against rising spot is information, not opportunity — and rebuts it with the $2.7B DOE enrichment commitment and the $80B Westinghouse term sheet. I verified both: they are real, and they were announced 2026-01-28 and 2025-10-28. The market has held that money for seven and eleven months and de-rated the equities anyway, so the rebuttal is stale by construction. Neither claim was cited in evidence or sources. The two evidence kinds are also one observation counted twice — technical_level and positioning both measure distance from the highs — so the supported conviction is 2. And the 58.97 target is 7.01 ATR out against a 6.0 guide while the scale plan trims two thirds before reaching it; at the 52.00 first trim the ratio is 1.27:1. It would also be the second position on the uranium driver alongside the open CCJ long, at a full 2% rather than sized as the pair its own key_risk instructs. The uranium view stays expressed through CCJ.

HAL KEPT, downgraded 4 -> 3, with three fixes. (1) The entry zone was unusable at both ends against the fixed 34.00 stop: at the old 38.20 top the ratio was 1.28:1, and the condition's claim that it 'stops clearing its floor' above 38.20 was wrong by a dollar — it stops at 37.20. At the old 36.00 bottom the stop was 1.81 ATR, inside the 2.0 ATR hard floor for a swing stock. Narrowed to 36.80-37.15, the only band satisfying both constraints; the 37.13 ideal, the 34.00 stop and the 43.59 target are unchanged, and no level was moved to rescue a ratio. (2) The counter_argument_answered evidence was cited to fortune.com/article/price-of-oil-09-09-2026, which I fetched: it contains none of the Houthi, Saudi-suspension, shut-in or China-restocking facts, reporting only Brent $102.05 up $2.20 with no driver given. The facts themselves are true and independently confirmed (NPR, Times of Israel, US News), so this is a re-sourcing rather than a kill — but the page also claimed the disruption 'takes quarters to restore', which the sources do not support: Saudi field teams were containing fires and assessing damage the same week, a days-to-weeks facility outage. What survives is the narrower laggard catch-up argument, held as macro beta. (3) Conviction 4 required three independent kinds and one of the three was a relative-strength observation labelled `positioning`; it is relabelled `technical_level`, which is what it is, leaving two genuine kinds and a supported score of 3. The real positioning data on HAL — 76.5% sell-side bullish, $17.7M of insider selling, zero buys — argues against the trade and sits in key_risk. HAL's key_risk also now names the live de-escalation track (Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor, Qatar back channel, US-Iran talks in Oman) rather than a hypothetical ceasefire headline, because a negotiated process already running is a materially different risk from a surprise.

THE FOUR EXITS ALL STAND and their `fail` verdicts are structural, not substantive: an exit has no target and no stop, so direction_consistency, risk_reward and stop_distance cannot compute by construction. TLT is the urgent one regardless of rank — a duration long into tomorrow's 08:30 CPI with 68% implied hike odds. LULU is settled by the company's own numbers. BCC's 12.50% spread flag is a pre-market artefact on a $23.8M ADV name and its key_risk already says to work the exit rather than dump it; its earnings_date flag is a false positive, since the catalyst is the LEN and KBH prints, not BCC's. NKE carried one factual error, now corrected: the page said its fiscal Q1 date was 'not on the fetched calendar, so NOT confirmed', but the validator read the same calendar and it carries NKE at 2026-09-28. The date is confirmed and 18 days out, so nothing scheduled sits between now and the exit. NKE remains the weakest of the four on its own admission, and worth naming: of its two evidence kinds, the `positioning` item is about LULU's guidance cut rather than about NIKE, so the NKE-specific case really is price alone.

NOT CUT, AND WHY NOT. The report's own arithmetic discipline held up under recomputation everywhere I checked it — the demotions to watchlist for XLE, XOM, LMT, LEU, GDX and BTC were each re-derived and each was correct, and no ratio was found nudged upward by a stretched target. The failures found were of a different kind: a bear case set too high, a source that did not carry its claim, an entry zone whose bounds contradicted its own stop, and a rebuttal built on old news. One new position out of a seven-idea report is a thin morning, and that is the honest reading of a tape where one supply shock drives four markets and almost everything else is pinned at an extreme.
